fixture_format: no patch: the repo at base_commit with every package installed (setup.sh `install`)

evals.name: repo-dependency-audit
evals.prompt: Can you audit the dependencies of this repo? I want to see how our packages depend on each other, what each one pulls in and by what type, how much things weigh, and what we should clean up first.
evals.expected_output: A structured report: all five packages, a Mermaid map, sizes, types, drift and prioritized recommendations; the repo left untouched.

assertions.text: Covers all five packages (server, client, reviewer-core, e2e, mcp-server) with prod/dev counts that match package.json: server 23/8, client 14/12, reviewer-core 2/4, e2e 0/3, mcp-server 2/5.

Contains a Mermaid diagram that shows the internal links: server -> reviewer-core (path alias), reviewer-core and mcp-server -> server's vendor/shared (path alias), client's mirrored copy of vendor/shared, and HTTP clients of the API (client and/or mcp-server).
Gives the installed node_modules size for each installed package, each within 25% of the measured value in ground_truth.json.
Distinguishes dependency types (prod vs dev, and runtime vs types vs build tooling) in the per-package detail.
Reports the zod major-version split: mcp-server on ^4 while server, client and reviewer-core are on ^3, and notes it matters because contracts are shared.
Names the heaviest client production dependencies with sizes, including next.
Flags @fastify/autoload in server as unused or removable, with evidence (modules are registered statically).
Ends with recommendations where every item has a priority (P0/P1/P2 or equivalent), the package, the dependency and a concrete action.
Leaves the repo untouched: no package.json, lockfile or node_modules change (git status clean after the run).
